english.title: Supervisor of provisional licence holder use hand-held mobile phone / device - endorsable offence
english.standardoffencewording:

(A)_[mobile telephone]_
(B)_[device of a kind specified in regulation 110(4))of the Road Vehicles (Construction and Use) Regulations 1986, namely **(..SPECIFY THE TYPE OF HAND HELD DEVICE..)]_

while supervising **(..SPECIFY THE NAME OF THE PROVISIONAL LICENCE HOLDER..), the holder of a provisional licence, who was driving a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 110(3) of the Road Vehicles (Construction and Use) Regulations 1986, section 41D of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) The scope of this offence was widened on the 25th March 2022 due to changes made by SI 2022/81. The changes mean that unless exceptions specified in the regulation apply, an offence will be committed at any time a mobile telephone or interactive communication device is used whilst driving (rather than just when the telephone/device was being used to perform an interactive communication function).
(ii) Statement of Facts procedure applies - see end of document for wording.
(iii) Fixed penalty scheme may be applied.
(iv) This is an endorseable offence , seeSchedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.
(v) Officers should note the defences to this offence, as provided by regulation 110(5) and (5A) and (5B) of the Road Vehicles (Construction and Use) Regulations 1986.IMPORTANT NOTE: The fixed penalty fine attributable to this offence increased from £100 to £200 on 1st March 2017. On the same date, the penalty points received for this offence increased from 3 to 6. For any offence committed before 1 March 2017, CJS Code RC86325 (H8695) should be used to reflect the penalty in force at the time of the offence.
